hypothesis: The 16 values per PPG SensorEvent are 16 consecutive time-samples of one channel (packed FIFO frame), not 16 distinct channels
test: Modify probe to dump all 16 values of consecutive events from one session; if time-samples, within-event values continue smoothly across event boundaries; if channels, each column stays constant across events
notes: Struct dump shows [signal, -32618, -4528, 0 x13]: only values[0] varies (the PPG sample), values[1..2] are constant across all 4 LED modes, values[3..15] always zero. Not time-samples.

hypothesis: The PPG sample rate delivered to the AP is fixed at ~25 Hz regardless of requested rate, because the sensor hub downsamples internally
test: Count events per 8 s session at requested rates 0/2000/4000/20000 us — all 4 PPG modes delivered n=195..202 (~25 Hz); wall-clock deltas show 5-event bursts every ~200 ms
notes: Every session = ~25 events/s with 1 sample/event; requested 500 Hz, delivered 25 Hz. Same for accelerometer. sysfs delay_ms writes (<handle> <ms>, format from HAL setDelay '%d %lld') also ignored: 250 Hz/1 kHz/100 Hz requests all delivered 25.6-25.9 Hz. Hub firmware hard-caps PPG output.

hypothesis: The sensor-hub binder service (IHmSensorHubService) is exported and bindable from a third-party app without signature permission, letting us trigger a heart-rate measurement
test: Check servicemanager registration and permission checks in decompiled client code
notes: hm_sensor_hub_service registered in live servicemanager; ServiceManager.getService works from apps (SELinux disabled). All transacts accepted. NOTE: requestHealthSensorHistoryData (code 9) with null dispatcher NPEs system_server (HmSensorHubMonitorService$DataHandler) - needs a real IDataDispatcher binder.

hypothesis: The raw-PPG file logging in sensors.sensorHub.so (/data/sensors/<ts>/ppg.txt) is gated by the debug.sensorhal.fill.block property; setting it enables HRV-grade raw PPG capture
test: setprop debug.sensorhal.fill.block 1, re-run the probe (activates PPG sensors), then check /data/sensors/ for ppg.txt with a high-rate raw stream
notes: /data/sensors never appeared. r2: the property is a fill-block debug switch (value length >= 55 makes setEnable return -EINVAL), not a logging gate.

hypothesis: The KLVP command used by enableAllDayHeartMonitor (sendKlvpRequest target=4, cmd=1, SportConfig field 42 mIsAlldayAutoHeartRateEnabled=true) starts continuous HR measurement in the sensor hub, making type-21 deliver BPM and getSensorDataInfo return live HR
test: Send the exact KLVP bytes [0xD0,0x02,0x01] via sendKlvpRequest from the probe app with the watch worn; poll getSensorDataInfo and type-21 events
notes: v5 probe on wrist: type-21 delivered 29 events in 40 s, BPM 84-92 (live pulse); raw PPG stream active simultaneously (ch0 41219-44603, ~25 Hz). Hub replies responseCode=90 (len=0); measurement starts regardless. Direct klvp.watch.so facade (v8) reproduces the same ack without the service.

hypothesis: The 25.8 Hz raw PPG stream (type 65538) contains a recoverable pulse when the all-day-HR measurement is active, sufficient for live HR + trend HRV with bandpass + peak detection
test: v10-v13 on-wrist runs: collect 65 s, bandpass (1.2 s MA trend removal + 3-pt smooth), peak detection with parabolic interpolation on wall clock, IBI outlier rejection
notes: v11: IBI clusters 558-644 ms (93-107 BPM) + 787-814 ms (76 BPM) = declining post-run pulse; median 610 ms -> 98 BPM. v13: steady HR 86-91 BPM resting. FFT confirms (1.76-1.90 Hz). Dicrotic notch causes double-detections (400 ms IBIs) - merge needed. RMSSD inflated by non-windowed analysis - sliding 55 s window fixes.

hypothesis: RMSSD is inflated because peak times use bursty callback arrival timestamps instead of the hub's uniform ~25.4 Hz sample clock
test: On one on-wrist capture, detect one common peak set and compute HR/RMSSD twice: callback wall timestamps vs reconstructed sample-index times; uniform timing must sharply reduce RMSSD while HR stays similar
notes: Same peaks, same cleaning: uniform clock RMSSD 36.9-40.7ms and SDNN 42-44ms; callback clock RMSSD 147-168ms and SDNN 97-101ms; HR unchanged 83.8-84.4 BPM. Root cause: five historical samples delivered per ~200ms callback burst. Final app uses fractional sample index * calibrated mean dt.

hypothesis: The four PPG handles (auto/25/40/55mA) sample on independent phase-staggered schedules, so simultaneous registration can produce an aggregate optical stream above 25 Hz
test: Register all four type-65538 sensors concurrently, measure per-stream and combined rates/arrival phases, then compare normalized on-wrist waveforms for phase offsets
notes: All four registrations returned true but all four delivered n=0 during 25s. Modes are mutually exclusive controls of one optical frontend; concurrent activation suppresses output rather than multiplying rate.

hypothesis: The world-writable sensorhub-channel-log or sensorhub-health character device emits the hub's internal high-rate PPG feed while all-day HR measurement is active
test: Start all-day HR through the proven direct KLVP path, then read sensorhub-channel-log, sensorhub-channel-common, sensorhub-health and sensorhub-algo and measure returned bytes
notes: health/algo return zero bytes; common is ioctl-only (read EFAULT); channel-log returns firmware diagnostic text (boot/flash logs), not PPG samples. It exposes W25Q16DW SPI flash and is useful for firmware RE.

hypothesis: The SensorHub diagnostic log exposes a hidden raw-PPG or sampling-rate command that can enable a stream above 25 Hz
test: Dump the complete sensorhub-channel-log buffer and search firmware diagnostics for PPG, ADC, sample-rate, raw-data, factory-test and debug command names
notes: Full 105KB diagnostic dump exposes ADPD174/PPG task logs, factory modes, HR algorithm and counters, but no raw-PPG or sampling-rate command. Channel-log is firmware text only; health/algo empty.

hypothesis: The ADPD174 sample period or output divisor is a patchable constant in sensorhub.bin, and changing it can raise the PPG task output above 25 Hz
test: Identify firmware architecture/base, locate ADPD174 init/task code and timing constants in the firmware, then validate addresses against live SDRAM using mcu_sdram before any flash
notes: Static RE: normal config sets REG_SAMPLING_FREQ 0x0050 (100Hz), REG_DEC_MODE 0x0220 (4x); factory table has 0x0004/0x0000 but Android PPG_TEST modes still output 25Hz. Traced REG_DEC_MODE writes to init/calibration paths; no host/live command found. Exact 2-byte patch is prepared but cannot be delivered rootlessly.

hypothesis: This 2019 kernel remains vulnerable to Dirty COW, allowing a two-byte patch to the read-only firmware without root
test: Run a static MIPS32 Dirty COW race for 20 million iterations against a harmless shell-owned 0444 file; contents must change
notes: Race ran ~137s and file remained unchanged. Kernel 3.10.14 has the Dirty COW backport; do not use against firmware.

hypothesis: A live SensorHub protocol command reaches firmware ADPD register 0x15 and can switch DEC_MODE from 0x0220 to 0x0000
test: Map firmware command dispatchers and all callers of the ADPD register-write primitive; identify a command whose handler writes register 0x15, then validate only its read/query path first

hypothesis: CVE-2014-3153 (Towelroot/futex) is exploitable on this MIPS32r1 3.10.14 kernel
test: Fingerprint futex implementation/config/patch state and build a MIPS32 prerequisite probe before any privilege-changing payload
notes: Correct FUTEX_CMP_REQUEUE_PI same-address probe returned -1/EINVAL on MIPS. The relevant requeue validation is patched; no Towelroot path.

hypothesis: CVE-2015-1805 (pipe splice) is exploitable on this MIPS32r1 3.10.14 Android kernel
test: Check pipe/splice syscalls and kernel config/patch indicators; run only a non-privilege-changing capability probe first

hypothesis: A writable system-uid or vendor service path gives root without a kernel exploit
test: Inventory exported system-uid components and verify caller-permission behavior with read-only binder/activity probes

hypothesis: A stock sport configuration type 14 changes the SensorHub ADPD output rate above 25 Hz
test: Call nativeConfigureSensorHubAlgorithm(0, Integer.valueOf(14)), measure PPG for 20 seconds, then stop with alg=3

hypothesis: The large RMSSD in the earlier live run came from bridging rejected intervals, not physiological variability
test: Run the current analyzer on captures/raw_ppg.csv and verify interval-level rejection does not bridge invalid neighbors; compare resulting RMSSD with the captured waveform's pulse spacing
notes: Captured 1507 samples: previous log had RMSSD 234.6ms with 39/55 clean intervals; corrected analyzer returns HR 81.24, RMSSD 25.34ms, SDNN 61.16ms, score 2.56%, clean 51/56. Invalid intervals no longer contribute an RMSSD pair.

hypothesis: The captured waveform's pulse timing is stable enough for a local regression fixture
test: Extract peaks from captures/raw_ppg.csv using reconstructed 25.24Hz sample time; valid IBI median and robust dispersion should match the analyzer's HR/RMSSD range
notes: Prominence-only adaptive detection finds 82 pulse peaks / 81 intervals with no implausible gaps. Intervals vary smoothly 596-857ms with paced ~0.1Hz respiratory sinus arrhythmia; local result HR 83.21, RMSSD 40.02ms, SDNN 70.37ms, coherence score 40.31%, clean 81/81. The old absolute-height threshold hid beats when baseline drifted negative.

hypothesis: The extra metric log after 'stopped: LED off' is a shutdown race in the two-second analysis loop
test: Exit immediately after the loop sleep when running was cleared by onPause; verify no analysis or UI update occurs after cleanup
notes: Device log showed t+79 metrics after the stop marker because stopAll ran during sleep. MainActivity now checks running immediately after sleep and exits before analyze().
